Final-round prep plan for Lincoln International, analyst role:
Timeline
- 3 days out: confirm the format (panel, case, or technical), who you meet, and the length. Re-read the job posting and map each requirement to a story from your experience.
- 2 days out: write out 5 to 6 stories in STAR form (situation, task, action, result), each with one number. Practice them out loud, timed at about 90 seconds each.
- 1 day out: drill the technical and case material for an analyst role (financial modeling basics, Excel, data interpretation, or whatever the posting names). Do two or three timed problems.
- Morning of: review your stories and your questions for them. Have your resume and their names ready.
Topics to cover
- Why Lincoln International and why this analyst role, specifically (their deal work, sector focus, and your fit).
- Behavioral: teamwork under pressure, handling a mistake, a time you disagreed with a manager, leadership without authority, a deadline you missed or nearly missed.
- Technical or case: the core skills the posting lists, walked through step by step, with your assumptions stated out loud.
- Your motivation and career path for the next two to three years.
What to practice
- Out loud, not in your head. Record yourself once and listen for filler words and rambling.
- Put a number in every story (dollars, percent, time saved, team size).
- Prepare two or three sharp questions for each interviewer about their work and how the team operates.

I don't have their company record or your resume on file yet, so I can't tailor this to their deal focus or your background. If you paste your resume, I'll build your stories from it. Which part of the final round is worrying you most: the behavioral questions or the technical or case portion?
